text:
alice: heads up — we are getting a bunch of customer reports with 401s during SSO logins and subsequent API calls since ~03:10 UTC. grafana: https://grafana.redwood.local/d/auth/auth-overview (spike on auth-introspect).
ben: seeing the alert too — auth-proxy 401 rate jumped from ~0.3% to ~8% at 03:09. traces point to token introspect failures (invalid_grant).
carol: any recent deploys or key rotations?
infra-bot: deploy-bot: auth-validate v2.14.1 rolled to prod at 2026-03-17T02:58:12Z by @deploy-pipeline
dana: we rotated the IdP signing cert at 03:06 as part of scheduled maintenance, and the IdP also changed assertion lifetime defaults (NotOnOrAfter now shorter). I flagged it but didn't expect immediate fallout.
eric: logs from auth-validate (prod):
```
2026-03-17T03:11:22Z auth-validate[request_id=abc123] WARN assertion validation failed: invalid_grant: assertion expired (NotOnOrAfter 2026-03-17T03:10:58Z)
2026-03-17T03:11:23Z auth-proxy[req=xyz789] ERROR introspect failed status=401 body={"error":"invalid_grant","error_description":"assertion expired"}
```
alice: support repro for a customer:
1) initiate SSO login via /oauth/saml/consume -> we get SAMLResponse back
2) POST to /oauth/token with assertion -> returns 401 invalid_grant
example curl we tested: 
```
curl -X POST https://auth.redwood.com/oauth/token -d grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:saml2-bearer -d assertion=<base64> 
# -> {"error":"invalid_grant","error_description":"assertion expired"}
```
carol: are API keys a usable fallback for affected customers?
dana: some enterprise accounts enforce SSO-only — no fallback. For others support can issue short-lived API keys but it's manual.
ben: quick mitigation idea: relax assertion freshness check in auth-validate for now (increase allowed skew) and restart pods. less risky than forcing IdP revert.
eric: verified in a staging repro — increasing MAX_ASSERTION_FRESHNESS to 180s accepts the assertion that was previously rejected.
alice: proposed hotfix: set MAX_ASSERTION_FRESHNESS=180 and rollout restart auth-validate. notify support to temp offer API keys for SSO-only customers where allowed.
dana: doing it now. command: `kubectl -n prod set env deployment/auth-validate MAX_ASSERTION_FRESHNESS=180 && kubectl rollout restart deployment/auth-validate`
infra-bot: kube: rollout restart started for deployment/auth-validate (12 pods to restart)
eric: observing 03:19 UTC after restart — auth-introspect 401s dropping, error rate at 0.6% and trending down.
carol: great. next steps for postmortem?
dana: action items: 1) contact IdP to revert or provide notice before changing assertion TTLs, 2) ship code change to make freshness knob more explicit and documented, 3) add alerting rule for sudden jump in assertion_expired errors, 4) support playbook update to include temporary API key procedure.
ben: add test in our CI that fails builds if assertion validation logic rejects expected short-lived assertions (simulate varying NotOnOrAfter).
alice: support to send a short notification to impacted customers: explain root cause, mitigation, and ETA for permanent fix. @carol can you own customer comms?
carol: on it — will draft and loop in legal/comms.
dana: I'll open a follow-up RFC for a more robust handling of IdP TTL drift and fallback logic.
eric: monitoring note: created dashboard panel and alert `HighAssertionExpiryRejections` to fire on >1% rate sustained for 3m.
alice: closing on slack thread — will update incident channel with postmortem link once RFC/retro complete. :white_check_mark:
